startup.name: Ruvo
startup.one_liner: The Global Dollar App for Brazil
startup.description: A global account for Brazilians to receive, hold and move money between USD and BRL, linking Pix, crypto and Visa. Personal (CPF) and business (CNPJ) accounts, yield on digital dollars. Team of 11 in Sao Paulo, formerly named Cacao, YC Summer 2025.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting rate of about 1 percent from references/yc_acceptance.md. Up for a team of 11 and a large local market with a clear cross border pain (dollar income, IOF tax, slow banks); down for a crowded neobank field and regulatory risk with no stated traction. Already listed in Summer 2025, so the ladder is the "if accepted" view.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say that dollar accounts for Latin America are a well worn idea with many funded rivals, and that the founders have not shown why they win against Wise, crypto exchanges and Nubank, nor how they handle Brazil banking rules around crypto.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry Fintech --calibration-only: seed 57% known only, 62% upper (n=23, anecdotal); B2B 2022-2025 seed 59% known only (n=126). Fintech median 10 months to seed.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 16.3 months, 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17. About 75 percent of eventual seeds land in that window, so the ever anchor of 0.57 gives about 0.43. I keep it flat: a team of 11 and a clear corridor help, while crypto rails in Brazil face regulatory uncertainty and many Latin American fintech seeds are under $1M or come from local funds. This number does not rank the company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels, a seed fund or a strategic. Most common when the product has early users but no paid base.
Institutional seed in the middle of the 2022 and later table, led by a seed fund after a few months of visible traction.
Larger institutional seed, usually needing paying customers or a standout team story and a competitive process.
Upside seed from a top tier fund in a hot category; rare and needs clear momentum.

ladder.why_it_fails: A consumer and small business fintech needs licenses, banking partners and compliance in Brazil, and the central bank was tightening rules on stablecoin cross border use through 2025 and 2026. Latin American stablecoin neobanks (Pana, Coco Wallet, Karsa) mostly raised small rounds or none that were public. Investors want a user and volume story, so without clear growth the company ends with the YC deal and small angel money below $1M.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series A 15% known only, 29% upper, cond 26% (n=74)
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window effect: Series A in fintech is late (about 16 months median from batch for those that reach it, with cond 23 percent in the Fintech cohort), and few months remain after a seed. The ever 0.23 to 0.26 scales to about 0.07.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed style round after slow revenue; sized like the lower quartile of 2022 and later rounds.
Core Series A near the 2022 and later median of $14M with a pre money in the market range of $50M to $65M.
Strong round after fast growth and a competitive process.
Hot category outlier round, similar to the largest AI Series A rounds.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A needs real transaction volume and regulatory clarity. Brazil is a competitive market with Nubank, Wise, Revolut and crypto exchanges all going after dollar accounts, and Latin American stablecoin neobanks such as Pana raised only seeds. Investors would likely wait for evidence that users keep dollars in the app.

anchors.source: same command: series B 2% known only, 18% upper, cond 16% (n=19)
anchors.adjustment_reason: Series B inside the window would need two more rounds in 16 months; the 0.16 conditional is cut by about three quarters.

bands.rationale: Flat or modest Series B because growth slowed.
Typical Series B near the 2022 and later median of $37M.
Upside Series B after strong growth, priced near the top of the 2022 and later table.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B requires proof that unit economics work at scale in a market with low take rates; only Aspora in the comparable set reached B and it did so with the Indian remittance corridor over about four years. The window leaves under a year after any Series A, and investors at that point would still be testing whether revenue repeats, so a second institutional round that fast would need growth well beyond what the analogs showed.

anchors.source: same command: series C 0% known only, 16% upper, cond 0% (n=3), too thin; used the all era calibration conditional of 36 percent (n=55) from references/stage_benchmarks.md and widened
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window effect: three further rounds in under two years almost never happens in the data, so the conditional of 0.25 is cut by more than half to reflect the short time left after a Series B.

bands.rationale: Modest Series C near the 2022 and later median of $45M.
Typical growth round for a company with clear category leadership and rising revenue.
Late stage upside round for a category leader, rare in the sample (n=9 since 2022).

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C inside the window would mean a breakout like the largest remittance companies, and licensing, FX costs and regulation make that path slow even for strong teams. Even if growth were exceptional, late rounds in this sample came years after the batch, and the 2022 and later Series C cell has only 9 rounds, so a Series C inside this window would be an extreme outlier.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most paths end in a stall or a small acquisition by an exchange or neobank. Regulatory change in Brazil, thin margins on FX and the need for local licenses make a large independent outcome unlikely, while a regional acquirer could buy the user base. Without a clear wedge or large revenue per customer the company is more likely to stall than to reach a meaningful sale.

killers.risk: Brazil central bank rules restrict crypto and stablecoin cross border flows
killers.evidence: The central bank was publishing rules on virtual asset providers in 2025, and Broad shut down while pursuing a similar Brazilian multicurrency product.
killers.mitigation: Use licensed partners and keep the fiat path through Pix and Visa as the core.

killers.risk: Strong incumbents and exchanges offer dollar accounts in Brazil
killers.evidence: OKX launched a Pix linked stablecoin card in Brazil and Nubank and Wise serve the same users.
killers.mitigation: Focus on freelancers and small businesses who earn in dollars.

killers.risk: Thin margins and fraud and compliance costs
killers.evidence: Remittance fees fall as competition grows (stablecoins cut cost by about 40 percent according to market sources).
killers.mitigation: Add yield and card interchange revenue.

killers.risk: Seed investors treat Latin American fintech cautiously
killers.evidence: Pana, Coco Wallet and Karsa show no large seeds despite years of operation.
killers.mitigation: Raise from LatAm and crypto funds that know the corridor.

technical_complexity.rationale: Pix integration, stablecoin custody, card issuing and KYC are all available through partners, so a small team can assemble the product in three months. The hard parts are licenses, fraud control, FX liquidity and compliance.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large players can add a dollar account in months but have been slow to; the startup depends on partner banks and on Brazilian rules, which creates a platform dependency.

evidence.claim: Brazil received about $318.8B in crypto flows from July 2024 to June 2025, mostly stablecoins, and freelancers use USDT to avoid the IOF tax on dollar inflows.

roadmap.goal: Prove users keep dollars in the account.
actions: Reach thousands of active freelancer accounts
Track average USD balances and repeat conversions
roadmap.proof: Monthly active accounts and balance per user growing

roadmap.goal: Raise a round above $1M within 16 months.
actions: Show monthly volume growth of 20 percent or more
Pitch LatAm fintech and crypto funds using volume and revenue per user
roadmap.proof: $5M or more monthly volume with positive take rate

roadmap.goal: Show a durable regulatory and unit economics position.
actions: Secure licenses or tier one partner banks in Brazil
Expand business (CNPJ) accounts for higher revenue per customer
roadmap.proof: $1M or more annual revenue at positive contribution margin

pros.point: Large real corridor with a tax and fee pain
pros.evidence: Dollar income earners in Brazil use stablecoins to avoid IOF and bank fees.

pros.point: Large team for a YC company
pros.evidence: Eleven people suggest a funded or revenue backed operation already.

brand.name: Ruvo
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Ruvo" --era 2022+: 4 characters, 1 word, invented or proper kind.
weaknesses: Says nothing about dollars or Brazil
Renamed from Cacao, which hints at a repositioning
brand.rationale: Short invented names are common among successful fintechs such as Nubank and Wise style brands, and a rename after YC shows the team is willing to fix brand issues. The name will not drive growth but does not hurt.

narrative.headline: A real corridor and a larger team than typical, but crowded and regulated; seed above $1M within 16 months is about the windowed base rate.
narrative.general_summary: Ruvo is a dollar account for Brazilians that connects Pix, stablecoins and Visa. Demand is clear: Brazil sees very large stablecoin flows and dollar earners pay fees and taxes. Competition is heavy, from Wise and Nubank to exchanges such as OKX that offered Pix linked cards. Comparable YC companies split: Aspora grew to Series B, Ping raised a large seed and went quiet, and Broad shut down. The window is 16.3 months so seed is the realistic outcome and later rounds are unlikely. The odds do not rank this company.

assumptions: Blind forecast from the YC listing only.
Window is 16.3 months, 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17. Local rounds in Brazil can be hard to find, which lowers confirmed seeds.
Fintech cohort has only 26 companies, so I also used the B2B anchor.
